title: Working in the houserules kit repository

entries.summary: Edit the kit in `template/`, then run `node bin/houserules.mjs update --dir .`; never hand-edit the root copies or the generated rules and skill.
body: This repository runs its own kit. The root copies of every `KIT_OWNED` path — `tools/`, `.claude/agents/`, and the kit skills — are the installed copy; `template/` is the source that `init` and `update` ship to every project.
`tests/dogfood.test.mjs` pins every root copy to its template source byte for byte; a hand edit fails the test and is lost on the next update.
`.claude/rules/*.md` and `.claude/skills/project-knowledge/SKILL.md` are generated by `tools/kb.sh render` from `knowledge/`.

entries.summary: Treat `~/projects/tag-pilot` as a read-only reference: never modify it, commit there, run its agents, or run `init` or `update` against it.
body: tag-pilot (branch `knowledge-management`, PR #42) is the origin of this kit and, until the adoption ruling in docs/design.md §5.4, the upstream of every kit-owned file.
Before every release, diff its `tools/`, `.claude/agents/`, and `.claude/skills/` against `template/` and port the drift; the first port is `process.evals-rerun` with its `co-change` check (HR-003).

entries.summary: Live-run every CLI change in a scratch `git init` repo: `init --dir <scratch>`, both checks inside; each gate its own `live_run` entry with `exit`.
body: Scratch repositories live under the session scratchpad, never inside this repository and never in tag-pilot. Run `tools/kb.sh check` and `tools/backlog.sh check` there and record each command’s verbatim output as its own report `live_run` entry (batch 3 task 3 recorded only one of a chained pair).

`pnpm dlx git+file://<this clone> files` exercises the published path (pnpm's bin shim execs the real file); `node <scratch>/node_modules/houserules/bin/houserules.mjs files` after `pnpm add --save-exact git+file://<this clone>` exercises the symlinked path (HR-001).
For a change to `update`, run `init` and then `update` in the same scratch repository and confirm that only kit-owned files changed.
The report names the scratch path (a `cd` entry or the path in the command) and records the init and both check gates as their own `live_run` entries; a live run without them fails the recipe.

A fix round that changes no CLI behavior (test-only, report-only, evidence wording) may stand on the task's original live run when the report discloses the scoping for the re-reviewer to judge (batch 6).

entries.summary: `node` and `pnpm` are on PATH only under `mise exec --` or `mise run` (`mise exec -- pnpm test`); without `mise.toml`, mise resolves no tools.
body: For a scratch directory, run tools as `mise x node@24.18.1 pnpm@11.18.0 -- <command>`; mise strips the paths of inactive tools, so a PATH export does not survive `mise x`.
The shipped wrappers `tools/kb.sh` and `tools/backlog.sh` use `node` from PATH and fall back to `mise exec node` on their own.

source.ref: session of 2026-08-31: mise could not exec npm in a scratch directory; probe of 2026-09-01

entries.summary: Relative to tag-pilot: unprefixed agent and skill names, `project-knowledge` skill, `dependency_vetting` for field `a19`, parameterized id prefix.
body: Agents: `tagpilot-implementer` → `implementer`, `tagpilot-task-reviewer` → `task-reviewer`, `tagpilot-branch-reviewer` → `branch-reviewer`. Skills: `tagpilot-orchestrating` → `orchestrating`, `tagpilot-knowledge` → `project-knowledge`.
Backlog ids: `TP-` → `--id-prefix` (default `WI`, `HR` in this repository). The install stamp is `.houserules.json`.
The kit was named lorekit until 2026-08-31; docs/design.md §5.1 records the rename.

entries.summary: The payload in `template/` runs on Node built-ins and POSIX shell only: no dependency, no build step; the CLIs work in a fresh clone before any install.
body: The SessionStart hook and the CI gates run where nothing is installed; a runtime dependency would break both (docs/design.md §2, option B).
This repository's devDependencies (vitest, commitlint) serve its own tests and commit hook only and never enter `template/`.
A template script may exec an optional tool only behind a probe of that tool itself, with a working fallback; probing mise or pnpm is not probing the tool (batch 6 task 4).

The shipped `.githooks/commit-msg` execs commitlint only behind a probe of `node_modules/.bin/commitlint` and degrades to the trailer gate alone; commitlint stays optional and never becomes a payload dependency.

entries.summary: Use pnpm for every package operation in this repository (`pnpm install`, `pnpm add --save-exact`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm dlx`); never `npm` or `npx`.
body: Owner ruling of 2026-09-01. The workspace follows tag-pilot: exact `node` and `pnpm` pins in `mise.toml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` as the only lockfile, the mise tasks `setup`, `test`, `lint`, and `audit`.
The payload in `template/` has no dependency and no install step (`houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins`); the ruling changes nothing there.

entries.summary: Vitest `restoreMocks` restores `vi.spyOn` spies only; reset a `vi.mock` factory’s `vi.fn` in an explicit `afterEach` with `mockReset()`.
body: `mockReset()` on a mock made with `vi.fn(impl)` also restores `impl` and drops queued `mockImplementationOnce` entries, so the wrapped real function comes back (verified against the Vitest 4 docs in the batch 3 task 1 fix round).
`tests/init.test.mjs` (the `vi.mock` factory for node:child_process and its `afterEach`) is the in-repo example.

source.ref: batch 3 task 1 review, critical 2; task-1-report.json docs_verified

entries.summary: When `KIT_OWNED` gains or loses a path, update README's agent-layer bullet and ownership table in the same commit.
body: README.md enumerates the kit-owned skills twice: the agent-layer bullet and the ownership-manifest table.
No test pins these enumerations; batch 5's task 1 review caught both stale after KIT_OWNED grew. A co-change check would misfire (bin changes without README constantly), so the rule stays judged.

entries.summary: globMatch in tools/kb.mjs is a union: matchesGlob for the full vocabulary, globToRegExp only for `**`/`*` with dot-segments; combining both matches neither.
body: node:path matchesGlob excludes a path segment that starts with `.` under `**` (undocumented; verified live on Node 24.18.1). globToRegExp restores dot-segments but translates only `**` and `*`, escaping every other metacharacter as a literal.

Write area and check globs with `**`, `*`, and literals only. Extend globToRegExp first if a glob ever needs `?`, `[ ]`, or `{ }` to cross a dot-segment; a mismatch is silent — the file simply drops out of the audit package.
When replacing a matching engine, pin the old engine's full vocabulary with counterexample tests before switching call sites (batch 6 task 1 round 1).

source.ref: batch 6 branch review; task 1 review round 0

entries.summary: release-please's config JSON schema omits prerelease-type and skip-snapshot from its root; keep those settings under packages['.'].
body: The schema at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/release-please/v17.11.2/schemas/config.json sets `additionalProperties: false` on the config root. The root's own `properties` list omits `prerelease-type` and `skip-snapshot`. `src/manifest.ts` reads both at the top level, like `versioning` and `release-type`. The project's docs show a top-level example with `prerelease-type`. The omission is a gap in the schema, not the runtime.

Verified with `ajv-cli validate`. A root-level `prerelease-type` key fails with `params.additionalProperty: 'prerelease-type'` (`must NOT have additional properties`). The identical key nested under `packages['.']` validates cleanly: that path's value schema (`ReleaserConfigOptions`, reached through `allOf`) carries no such restriction.

Put `prerelease-type`, `skip-snapshot`, and the other release settings under `packages['.']` in `release-please-config.json`, not at the config root. `src/manifest.ts` merges each package's config over the root default per key, so a single-package repository behaves identically either way. Only the nested placement passes the schema the file's own `$schema` points at.

entries.summary: Every test that mints a scratch directory registers its removal at the mkdtemp site: the shared helper, or onTestFinished/afterEach with recursive rmSync.
body: At the batch 9 task 2 review, tests/ held 21 mkdtempSync call sites across seven test files with no cleanup; a full suite run left /tmp holding 1714 orphaned houserules-target-* trees plus 89 kb-* and 15 ws-* trees, and a transient inode exhaustion had already broken one suite attempt.

The suite leaves the temp root as it found it: call tests/scratch-dir.mjs's scratchDir(prefix), which mints the directory and registers rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }) on onTestFinished. A site that cannot use the shared helper registers the same removal itself, in an explicit onTestFinished or afterEach.

source.ref: batch 9 task 2 review; batch 9 branch review rider; HR-035

entries.summary: After a release-please PR merge, run update --dir ., commit the restamp, and push; see docs/runbook.md.
body: release-please bumps package.json's version in its PR. Merging that PR does not update .houserules.json. The stale stamp fails tests/dogfood.test.mjs's exact-equality pin on main (HR-044).

After you merge a release-please PR: run `mise exec -- node bin/houserules.mjs update --dir .` (it prints the drift line, for example `kit 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0-alpha`); commit the restamped `.houserules.json` as `chore(release): restamp the kit version`; push to main.
Full steps and rationale: docs/runbook.md.

In a project that installs the kit: run the package manager's install first (the exec otherwise runs the still-installed old copy and reads no drift), then `pnpm exec houserules update --dir .`, and commit `.houserules.json` only when the drift line's sides differ. The finishing-a-feature skill ships this form; pnpm 11's verifyDepsBeforeRun=install default can mask the stale-copy state in reproductions (batch 13 task 1).
